issues.what: First Sealand dynasty keyframes -1600 (-1600..-1501) and -1500 (-1500..-1401) carry the 42-50 E x 27-32.3 N box (1,599 cells); the Sealand would fall back from 179 cells to the box at -1600; babylonia_-1600 and -1500 cut the same box from Babylonia. Already settled: m1600-m1501 keyframe_overrides/0 and /1 (written 2 Nov 20:28) and m1500-m1401 keyframe_overrides/0, /1, /4 and events/1, /2 replace the box by the marsh shape plus Dhi-Qar, Basra, Uruk, Nippur and Isin and cut Babylonia by the same land; the published drafts of 22:32 on 2 Nov carry them.

Carchemish was drawn untinted to 717 after m0900-m0801 events/0 closed its Assyrian tint at -848; the pages date its tribute to Tiglath-Pileser III: Pisiri 'was tributary to the Assyrian king Tiglath-Pileser III' in 738 (the Tiglath-Pileser III page puts the tribute of Gurgum, Kummuh, Carchemish and Quwe after Arpad fell in 740, undated). Added a vassal_start of 738 on the dossier's own 60 km region; the dossier's vassal_end of 717 closes it.

Sam'al was drawn untinted to 717 after m0900-m0801 events/1 closed its tint at -824; the Sam'al page and the Tiglath-Pileser III page are silent on the 8th-century vassalage. The Zincirli Expedition page dates it: Tiglath-pileser III 'installed Panamuwa II on the throne of Sam'al' in the campaign of 743-740 (Panamuwa II killed fighting alongside the Assyrians at Damascus in 733/732; Barrakib 'the servant of Tiglath-pileser'). Added a vassal_start at -740 (the end of the page's range) on the dossier's 40 km region; the dossier's vassal_end of 717 closes it.

Side effect of m0900-m0801 events/0 and /1 that the reporting agent did not see: with the two tints closed, the Neo-Assyrian -800 and -750 keyframes (Cliopatria's shape, which covers both states) take Carchemish's 22 cells (R2: both dossiers name the Neo-Assyrian Empire as successor) and 10 of Sam'al's 19 as direct land at -800, so both vanish from the map to 717; without a -750 override a second snap takes 39 cells at -750 (tested). Overrides keep both off Assyria's shape while independent (Carchemish page: absent from Assyrian sources from Samsi-Adad V to the mid-8th century; Sam'al page: independent after Shalmaneser III's death). Sam'al's whole 40 km circle is cut; for Carchemish only its own 22 cells (60 km circle intersected with a polygon north of the Til Barsip land), because the circle also holds 18 cells Assyria took with Bit Adini in 856 and a first cut of the whole circle released them (snap 'removed 20').

neo-hittite-states keeps its 31-cell vassal tint of Assyria from -868. Reviewed together with the -800 overlap: the tint is not the basis of Carchemish and Sam'al any more (they are carved out and drawn on their own), and the aggregate lists the Neo-Assyrian Empire as successor, so without the tint R2 would hand its remaining cells (Amuq/Pattin and the edges of the hull) to Assyria as direct land. The pages opened say nothing on those lands before the Arpad (740) and Pattin (738) entries, which the ledger already has; the tint is left as drawn.

dossier_requests.what: identity.successors names neo-assyrian-empire for the whole life (also sam-al, neo-hittite-states and bit-agusi), so R2 gives Assyria their land whenever an Assyrian keyframe covers it, years before the state ends (Carchemish and Sam'al independent until 738/740, Arpad until 740).
